The strict inequality is enforced in one place over both the record and each layer, the layer-may-not-spell-a-unit rule falls out of the unknown-key refusal and is asserted by its own message ('second-spelling'), and the tightness negative control (an optional key set to another legal value is ACCEPTED) is present, so the refusals are not a validator that reds on any edit.

The recomputation is real and the declared mutation has teeth exactly as recorded: min(lows) -> max(lows) in combine() reds 3 - the envelope row and BOTH rows about the committed example record on disk - while the AC2 positive control stays green because it compares the record against the same broken combine(), which the fragment says in writing. The widen/do-not-narrow pair is measured through the real build_record, the unknown rule is refused in the validator AND in combine() with the declared set in the message, and the empty layer set is refused in both. A hand-widening of one token and a hand-narrowing of a thousand are both refused with the claimed pair and the computed pair in the text.

The strongest criterion of the five, and the `inputs` work is genuinely exhaustive rather than exhaustive-sounding: I checked validate._scalar's four coercions (inline list, inline map, quote-stripping, integer) against _render_scalar's four refusals and they cover each other, so the writer really is bound to the reader rather than agreeing with it by luck. TWO NOTES. (1) M8d, the anti-emptying binding, reds its row and then kills the entire selftest process with an uncaught KeyError at fragment line 477, so every row after it - all of AC4 and AC5 - is never evaluated in that state (finding F9). (2) The module docstring's claim under this schema, 'The filename IS the key', is FALSE for a spec id carrying a path separator, and that is finding F1, the review's first blocker.

Every property AC4 names holds and every declared mutation reds its own row: dropping PROTECTED_REWORK reds the protected-touch row alone (1); recording a scale that is not the one used reds the inputs-reproduce-the-bounds row alone (1); propose() stamping date.today() reds 3, and its indirect variant reds 2 with the text property honestly staying green; build_record hardcoding the date reds 2 even when hardcoded to the fixture's own date. The load-bearing pair is a real measurement with real teeth, and it survives an adversarial route. ONE CLAUSE IS UNEVIDENCED: 'Nothing in scripts/verify.sh calls this module' is proven by a slot-value scan plus two substring absences, and a required stage reached by a computed path walks straight past all three - see F4. findings.text: THE WRITER ESCAPES ITS OWN DIRECTORY AND SILENTLY DESTROYS A PROTECTED FILE. validate_record checks `spec` only as a non-empty string, and write_record joins it straight into a path: `d / ("%s.yaml" % rec["spec"])`. So a record whose spec is `../policy` is VALID and writes outside .veldo/estimates. This is reachable through the sanctioned CLI over a spec the contract validator itself accepts: validate.py format-checks PLAN ids (`PLAN-\d+`) and does NOT constrain a spec id, so `id: ../policy` gives check_spec 0 errors. The overwrite guard does not help, because it only refuses to overwrite an existing ESTIMATE; anything else at that path is replaced without a word and without --replace. The schema's own premise, 'The filename IS the key, so two estimates for one spec cannot exist', is false for such an id, and estimate_for reads it back through the same traversal. This repository already ships the correct shape for exactly this defect: claim.py's unit_id_problem / ledger_basename, added under ledger finding 49, put the refusal in the one place that knows the id-to-path mapping so no caller can route around it.
findings.evidence: In a throwaway tree that is a copy of .veldo, with a spec carrying `id: ../policy`: `python3 .veldo/estimate.py propose --spec specs/evil.md --at 2026-08-13 --write` printed `wrote /tmp/trav1402run/.veldo/estimates/../policy.yaml` and exited 0. .veldo/policy.yaml went from 3977 bytes / first line `schema: veldo.policy/v1` to 849 bytes / first line `schema: veldo.estimate/v1`. Separately: validate.check_spec on that spec = 0 errors; E.validate_record(build_record('../victim/OWNED', ...)) = []; write_record returned <tmp>/estimates/../victim/OWNED.yaml resolving outside the estimates directory, and estimate_for('../victim/OWNED') read it back. Log PART 4. FIX SHAPE: refuse in validate_record a `spec` that is not its own basename (reuse claim.unit_id_problem rather than spelling a second character rule), and assert in write_record that the resolved path is inside the records directory; one row per half, with the additive control that a normal id still writes.

findings.text: THE CONFIDENT ZERO IS IN THE RECORD'S OWN FEATURE READ, AND IT IS LIVE ON THIS REPOSITORY. toe_corpus.footprint_of matches `^footprint:\n((?:\s+-\s+.*\n)+)`, so it requires the line after `footprint:` to be a list item and stops at the first line that is not one. A COMMENT inside the block therefore truncates the read, and a comment on the FIRST line empties it. The record then states `regression_surface: 0` and `protected_touch: no` as measurements - the input was recorded, and the module reports zero, which is exactly the class PLAN-0018's C1 names. MEASURED: 8 of 214 specs get a materially wrong committed record, and 3 of them state protected_touch: no about a spec that DOES touch a declared protected path - which is the one feature the model's own comment calls 'the one mechanical feature of a spec that reliably predicts a wait on a person'. VELDO-0010 is the worst: 13 declared footprint entries including scripts/verify.sh and engine/scripts/verify.sh, read as 0, committed as 120000-750000 where the correct read gives 375000-2344000, a 3.1x understatement. The reader is WARP-1401's and the repair belongs there, but WARP-1402 is the item that publishes the number as a record three later items write into and W5 reconciles against, and its AC4 row blesses surface 0 for 'a spec with NO footprint block' without ever distinguishing an unreadable block from an absent one.

Records at HEAD vs correct: VELDO-0010 0/no/120000-750000 -> 13/yes/375000-2344000; WARP-0722 0/no/120000-750000 -> 15/yes/460000-2875000; WARP-0727 10/yes/500000-3125000 -> 20/yes/750000-4688000. CONTROL A4: applying the two-line fix (drop full-line comments before the regex) leaves this suite at 46 passed 0 failed and the WHOLE repository at 4723 passed, 0 failed - so no assertion anywhere is about either answer. Log PART 6. FIX SHAPE: skip comment lines in footprint_of, plus one row here over a fixture spec whose footprint block carries a comment requiring the surface to equal the block's item count, and a refusal (or a named stand-down) when a footprint block is present but reads empty.

findings.text: A LIVE-STATE PIN WHOSE REQUIRED ANSWER IS THAT THIS REPOSITORY STAYS BROKEN. The AC4 MEASURED row requires policy_tier('critical')[2] == 'default', which is true only because .veldo/policy.yaml writes the critical tier across two lines and the ONE parser folds the continuation into the preceding scalar. Repairing that - putting the same inline map on one line, changing no meaning - turns the row RED, and CHECK_unit runs the full selftest as a required stage, so a correct repair of the file this item's own docstring calls out reddens the whole gate. This is ledger finding 51's shape: the right fix is to assert the PROPERTY the pin stands in for (every record states which source it got, and the source it states is the source it used) rather than to pin today's answer for one tier. The hermetic one-line fixture control beside it is good and should carry the whole weight; the live half adds a pin and no property.

findings.text: THE RECORD DOES NOT NAME THE MODEL THAT PRODUCED IT, so the reconciliation this schema exists to enable can refit the scale and not the structure. The layer's inputs carry structural_weight_tenths, tokens_per_structural_unit and spread_pct, but NOT BASE_TENTHS, AC_TENTHS, SURFACE_TENTHS, GATE_REWORK or PROTECTED_REWORK, and no version field stands for them. The docstring's claim, that W5 can 'tell a good estimate (weight right, scale right) from a lucky one' and 'refit the scale without touching the structure', holds only while the coefficients never change; the moment one does, an old record's weight cannot be decomposed and no reader can tell which model produced which record. The suite's own reproduction row reads the coefficients from the MODULE, not from the record, so it agrees with itself by construction and cannot see this. This is cheap now and expensive the day records exist, which is the argument the spec itself makes for defining the schema here in full.
findings.evidence: Read: structural_proxy's returned inputs map contains 13 keys, none of them BASE_TENTHS / AC_TENTHS / SURFACE_TENTHS / GATE_REWORK; RECORD_REQUIRED and RECORD_OPTIONAL declare no model or version field. Suite row 'THE LAYER'S RECORDED INPUTS ARE SUFFICIENT TO REPRODUCE ITS OWN BOUNDS' recomputes the weight as (E1402.BASE_TENTHS + E1402.AC_TENTHS * ... + E1402.SURFACE_TENTHS * ...) * cycles, i.e. from module constants, so changing a coefficient moves both sides together and the row cannot fail for it. FIX SHAPE: one more input key naming the coefficient set (or the three tenths values), which W5 then reads instead of importing today's constants.

summary: SHIP VERDICT: DO-NOT-SHIP this commit as it stands, and the reason is three blockers, not a soft one among them. FAIL. (1) F1: the writer escapes its own directory. validate_record checks `spec` only as a non-empty string and write_record joins it into a path, so `python3 .veldo/estimate.py propose --spec <a spec whose id is ../policy> --at ... --write` replaced .veldo/policy.yaml, a declared PROTECTED path, with an estimate record - 3977 bytes to 849, first line `schema: veldo.policy/v1` to `schema: veldo.estimate/v1` - with no --replace and no refusal, over a spec validate.check_spec itself accepts with 0 errors. In a stranger's repository that is a shipped tool destroying a file it was never asked to touch. (2) F3: the record reports a number it did not measure. toe_corpus.footprint_of stops at the first non-item line, so a comment inside a footprint block truncates or empties the read, and the record then states regression_surface and protected_touch as measurements: 8 of this repository's 214 specs get a materially wrong record and 3 of them say protected_touch: no about specs that touch protected paths. VELDO-0010 declares 13 footprint entries including both verify.sh copies, reads as 0, and commits 120000-750000 where the correct read gives 375000-2344000. Fixing the reader reds nothing anywhere in 4723 assertions, so nothing is about either answer. (3) F2, which inverts the ship question rather than answering it: holding this module back is ALSO broken. sizing_pass.py, toe_analogy.py, toe_reconcile.py and toe_budget.py all load .veldo/estimate.py and all four already ship, so the composed claude pack answers three of their commands with FileNotFoundError: .veldo/estimate.py - and the exclusion's stated reason, 'W3, W4, W5 and W8 are still to build', is false against a tree that contains all four modules and two of their suites. So the right move is not more withholding: fix F1 and F3, then ship estimate.py together with toe_normalize.py, lay both down in init_scaffold and declare the capability, or withhold all six PLAN-0014 modules as one set. WHAT IS SOLID, and it is most of the item: 13 of 13 declared falsifications have teeth and red exactly the rows they name, including the four self-inflicted defects the fragment records honestly, the negative that reverting only the renderer reds nothing, and a hardcoded date equal to the fixture's own date still reddening because the binding is two distinct dates over one spec. The `inputs` state table is exhaustive against the parser's actual coercions rather than exhaustive-sounding. AC5's load-bearing three-way check_spec measurement survived an adversarial route through a computed path and went red as it should. And the additive control passes at full scale: committing two real estimates through the sanctioned CLI leaves the whole repository at 4723 passed, 0 failed, so this item does not carry the live-state pin that reddens when a feature is used - except in one place, F5, where it requires this repository's policy.yaml to stay unreadable for the critical tier, and F4, where a required gate stage that blocks work on an estimate leaves this suite green and only a sibling item's derived gate domain catches it. Three blockers, three majors, three minors.
